nodes.question: How does the process of balancing policy options and integrating them into packages help in policymaking?
nodes.answer: Balancing policy options and integrating them into packages allows for defining, redefining, and balancing policy packages, especially when legal feasibility depends on combining various policy instruments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Peace, justice and strong institutions|Good governance|Policy coherence mechanisms_qna_001
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are some drawbacks of policy integration mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Drawbacks of policy integration include high transaction costs and potential unintended side effects due to unpredictable risks in a complex multi-sector setting.

Likewise, when implementing policies, actors can plan their activities over one speci C problem or over multiple societal challenges (Lyles et al. 2018 ). While most studies tend to focus on the system level interacting effects(e.g. Duguma et al., 2014 ; Berry et al. 2015 ), and speci - cally address policy integration (Di Gregorio et al. 2017 ; Cejudo & Trein 2023 ; Biesbroek, Candel 2020 ), this research focuses on the operational level of integration, where solutions have a physical impact. Notwithstanding these bene its, researchers also admit that integration can imply high transaction costs and may have unintended side effects due to the impossibility of predicting the risks in such a complex multi-sector setting (Bryson et al. 2006 ; M rker et al. 2018 ; Kongsager 2018 ; Metz et al. 2020 ). In addition, De Lo and Patterson ( 2017 p. 93) state that challenges for which causes, effects, and interests are relatively clear, uncontentious, and bound by sector are generally tackled most ef ciently using a sectoral scope.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why was the decision made to categorize each policy by the dominant type in each dimension?
nodes.answer: The decision was made to simplify the mapping process and avoid duplication of policies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Peace, justice and strong institutions|Good governance|Policy coherence mechanisms_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is it important for policy mixes to be consistent, coherent, and aligned?
nodes.answer: Policy mixes need to be consistent, coherent, and aligned to avoid problem-shifting and conflicting aims across policy fields and levels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Peace, justice and strong institutions|Good governance|Policy coherence mechanisms_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do policy designs evolve over time according to Howlett, Mukherjee, and Rayner (2018)?
nodes.answer: Policy designs evolve through processes such as layering, stretching, patching, and packaging, showcasing the dynamic nature of policy development and implementation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Peace, justice and strong institutions|Good governance|Policy coherence mechanisms_qna_005
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the main argument presented regarding interactive governance in the administrative sector?
nodes.answer: The main argument is that while intersectoral interaction is emphasized, it is also crucial to improve interaction within the administrative sector itself to overcome coordination problems caused by the strict separation of different public administrations.
nodes.paragraph: While the accent in the debate on interactive gover- nance is on the intersectoral, it is equally important to strive for more interaction within the administrative sector itself. The concern with this task is often debatedin terms of challenging the strict separation of different public administrations as silos (Scott & Gong, 2021 ). This leads to coordination problems due to theindividual perspectives and priorities of each organisa- tional unit, which do not share this information (Bogumil & Jann, 2020 ; Hustedt & Radtke, 2024 ). This is particularly evident when a new eld of action such as climate politics emerges, challenging already existing goals and routines across policy areas anddepartments. A shift towards a more co-operative style of action requires reorientation and restructuring steps on allsides (Tuurnas et al., 2023 ) stakeholders and admin- istrators, citizens and politicians. Political organisations and bodies (local councils and elected of cials) as wellas administrations need to open up statehood further to stakeholders from civil society and business. Likewise, civil society organisations cannot just simply regard themselves as a counter-power limiting itself toorganising pressure from below or from outside .
